Where it began

Zaheer Khan was born in 1978 in Shrirampur, in the Ahmednagar district of Maharashtra. He learned the game under the coach Utsav Yadav and with the local Revenue Colony club, then moved on to Pune and, in 1996, to Mumbai, where he joined the National Cricket Club. A spell of 7 for 74 in the Purshottam Shield in January 1997 got him noticed.

His club owner sent him to the MRF Pace Foundation in Chennai, and the coach there, T. A. Sekhar, steered him towards Baroda. In the Ranji Trophy final of 2000–01 he was man of the match, helping Baroda to their first title in 43 years. In 2000 he was also in the first intake at the National Cricket Academy in Bangalore.

The player

He made his Test debut against Bangladesh in 2000. Over 92 Tests up to 2014 he took 311 wickets at 32.95, with a best of 7 for 87, 11 five-wicket innings and one ten-wicket match. By November 2026 only Kapil Dev had taken more Test wickets among India's pace bowlers.

His greatest days came in one-day cricket. He helped India to the 2003 World Cup final, and at home in 2011 he led the attack, sharing the honour of top wicket-taker with 21 as India lifted the trophy. Wisden made him one of its Cricketers of the Year in 2008.

What made him special

He could move the ball both ways, and he was a master of reverse swing once the shine had gone. Left-handers found him a particular puzzle: Matthew Hayden, Sanath Jayasuriya, Kumar Sangakkara and Graeme Smith each fell to him more than 10 times in international cricket.

Nobody picked him for his batting, though for some years the highest Test innings ever played by a last man was his: 75 against Bangladesh in 2004. Sachin Tendulkar was at the other end, and together they put on 133, then an Indian record for the tenth wicket.

Away from the middle

In county cricket he took ten wickets on his debut for Worcestershire in 2005. Later he captained Delhi in the IPL. In 2014 he founded ProSport Fitness and Services in Mumbai, a training centre for athletes and others. After his playing days he moved into coaching: bowling consultant to India, Director of Cricket for Mumbai Indians from 2018, mentor at Lucknow, and, from September 2026, head coach of Chennai Super Kings.

He received the Arjuna Award in 2011 and the Padma Shri in 2020. In 2017 he married the actress Sagarika Ghatge.

And finally

Before the 2011 World Cup he spent a year working on a knuckle ball and then kept it hidden, refusing to use it in any match until the tournament began. Most bowlers cannot wait to show off a new trick. He waited a whole year, and the wickets of a World Cup were his reward.
